rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He connects the martyrs’ promised life with the Qur’anic account of Pharaoh’s family being shown the Fire, citing both passages as descriptions of postmortem experience.
rows.anchor: âyetiyle وَرَحْمَةٌۭ’lerde Âl-i Fir‘avn hakkında:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that souls are distinct conscious substances apart from bodies and remain perceptive after death.
rows.anchor: rûhların başlı başına kāim ve mahsüs olan cevher-i bedenden başka birer cevheri bulunduğuna ve bunun ba‘de’l-mevt müdrik olarak kaldığına

rows.speaker: Cumhûr-ı sahâbe ve tâbi‘în
rows.claim: The majority of the Companions and Successors also hold that the soul persists consciously after death.
rows.anchor: Cumhûr-ı sahâbe ve tâbi‘în rıdvanullâhi ‘aleyhim ecma‘în hazarâtının da kavilleri budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage singles out martyrs to signal the elevated rank they have with God.
rows.anchor: burada bunun şühedâya tahsîsi makamlarının ‘indallah yüksekliğini iş‘âr içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam’s account of the hereafter is not exhausted by this postmortem state; resurrection and new creation also complete the doctrine.
rows.anchor: İslâm’da mes’ele-i âhiret bundan ibaret değildir. Bunu daha ziyade tavzîh ü itmam edecek olan mes’ele-i ba‘s, halk-ı cedîd

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At this point the verse indicates the grave and the intermediate realm after death and before resurrection.
rows.anchor: Burada henüz mevti tâkip eden kabir ve âlem-i berzah meselesine işaret buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported view says the verse was revealed about the fourteen martyrs of Badr.
rows.anchor: şühedâ-yı Bedir hakkında nâzil olduğuna dâir bir kavil vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He considers it more likely that the verse prepared the community after the change of qibla and before the Battle of Badr.
rows.anchor: tahvîl-i kıbleyi müte‘akib ve gazâ-yı Bedir’den mukaddem bir ihzar olması daha ziyade melhuzdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trials are meant to distinguish those who follow the Prophet and to complete the blessing bestowed on them.
rows.anchor: Peygambere ittibâ‘edip etmeyeni seçmek ve o nimeti itmam etmek üzere sizi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers taste worldly trials so that they may attain the promise that they will have no fear or grief in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: sırrına ermeniz için dünyada biraz bu mihnetleri tadacaksınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trials include fear of enemy attack, hunger from famine and scarcity, loss of wealth and life through war and its expenses, and loss of earnings or children.
rows.anchor: düşmanların hücûmu korkusu, kıtlık ve darlıktan dolayı açlık, muharebe ve mesârif-i muharebe dolayısıyla mal, can eksikliği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general wording also alludes to obligations: fear to fearing God, hunger to Ramadan fasting, loss of wealth to zakat, loss of lives to jihad, martyrdom and illness, and loss of crops to children and earnings.
rows.anchor: Havf Allah korkusuna, açlık ramazan orucuna, mal eksikliği zekâta, nüfûs eksikliği cihâd ü şehâdete ve emrâza

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Limited trials prevent such hardships from taking over universally and lead to great blessings in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: her birinden böyle birazcık ibtilâ ile mükellefiyet bunların küllî ve umûmî surette istîlâlarına mâni‘olacak ve âhirette büyük büyük nimetlere îsâl edecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to give glad tidings to those who remain patient.
rows.anchor: Yâ Muhammed! Sen sabr edenleri ise müjdele

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a Prophetic hadith teaching that anything which hurts a believer is a calamity for that believer.
rows.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfi mûcebince ezâ verecek herhangi bir zarara giriftâr oldukları zaman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When any harmful loss befalls them, the patient say the formula of belonging to God and returning to Him, finding comfort through submission.
rows.anchor: Allah’a arz-ı teslîmiyet ile mütesellî olarak sabrederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say this not only with their tongues but wholeheartedly, reflecting on the purpose of creation.
rows.anchor: bunu yalnız lisânen değil, gāye-i halk u hilkati düşünerek bütün kalb ile söylerler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that they belong to God acknowledges that all property and selves belong to Him and that His will over them cannot rightly be challenged; this is acceptance of divine decree and the station of the contented soul.
rows.anchor: emvâl ü enfüs her şeyi Allah’a teslim ve Allah teâlâ’nın milki olan her şeyde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying that they return to God affirms death and eventual return, while hoping for divine acceptance and union rather than absolute nonbeing; this is the station of the soul pleasing to God.
rows.anchor: gayenin ‘adem-i mutlak olmayıp visâl-i küllî olduğuna iman ve bu iman ile ‘indallah marzî olmak ümidini izhar vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through religious knowledge and Prophetic ethics the soul rises through five stages: commanding, self-reproaching, tranquil, content, and pleasing to God.
rows.anchor: İnsanın nefsi ibtidâ nefs-i emmâre iken ma‘ârif-i dîniye ve ahlâk-ı Muhammediye ile terakki ederek sâniyen nefs-i levvâme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine address in al-Fajr describes the contented and divinely approved soul returning to its Lord.
rows.anchor: hitâb-ı ilâhîsi bunun beyânıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Return to God is not movement toward a place or direction, since God is transcendent beyond both.
rows.anchor: Bu rücû‘un bir mekân ve cihete intikal suretiyle olmadığı âşikârdır. Zira Allah teâlâ cihet ü mekândan münezzehtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He presents three possible senses of return: a figurative confession of annihilation, a confession of subsistence, or an acknowledgment of both in different respects.
rows.anchor: 1. Bu, nefsimiz hakkında bir ikrâr-ı fenâdan kinayedir. 2. İkrâr-ı bekādır. 3. Min vechin fenâ ve min vechin bekāyı ikrardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He chooses the third sense: affirming our essential passing away and our subsistence only through God.
rows.anchor: Bizce doğrusu bu üçüncüsüdür. Zira hepimizin fenâ-yı zâtîsi ile bekā-billâhı ikrardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As at our origin, after death we will exist only in divine knowledge and decree, not through existence that is our own.
rows.anchor: yine onun gibi yok olacağız ve olduğumuz gibi yalnız ilm-i ilâhîde ve sırf hükm-i ilâhîde mevcud kalacağız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are born with their innate endowments before acting, but die carrying what they have earned, good or bad, and bearing responsibility.
rows.anchor: giderken ise iyi veya kötü kazanacağımızı kazanmış, iyilik veya kötülük nâmına neyimiz varsa hepsini omuzumuza almış, mes’ûliyeti yüklenmiş olarak gideceğiz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Our essence rests on divine knowledge, existence on God’s existence, and continuance on divine subsistence; return means enduring through God in a manifestation of beauty or majesty.
rows.anchor: zâtımız ilm-i ilâhî ile, vücûdumuz vücûd-i ilâhî ile, bekāmız da bekā-yı ilâhî ile kāim olur.

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi reads the return as referring to the hereafter: in this world people appear to control benefits and harms, but after death only God’s judgment governs them.
rows.anchor: Râzî diyor ki “Bu rücû‘âhirete işârettir. Biz dünyada iken az çok kendimiz veya başkaları da menfaat ve mazarratımıza zâhiren mâlik bulunuyorduk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This return entails resurrection, gathering, and other afterlife judgments through a new creation; the true hereafter is the eternal life after resurrection.
rows.anchor: halk-ı cedîd ile ba‘s, haşr ü neşr ve sâir ahkâm-ı uhreviye terettüb edebilecektir. Ve asıl âhiret ba‘sten sonraki hayât-ı ebediye olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The return in this verse also covers the interval after death and before resurrection, which some explain as the soul’s continued existence.
rows.anchor: buradaki rücû‘mevtten sonra ve ba‘sten evvelki hâlete de şâmildir, buna bazıları “bekā-yı rûh” nâmını vermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “soul’s continued existence” suggests self-subsistence, while return to God entails acknowledging essential annihilation and therefore means more than that.
rows.anchor: “bekā-yı rûh” tâbirinde bir bekā-yı zâtî şâibesi vardır, rücû‘da ise fenâ-yı zâtîyi itiraf münderictir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the body perishes and the soul may persist for a time, at the great Resurrection even souls may perish; 28:88 states that all perishes except God’s Face, while the reality known to God is never lost and can be recreated.
rows.anchor: zâtîmiz ez-her cihet tahakkuk edeceği ve ancak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether the reality known to God is soul, body, both, or something beyond them, any continued existence is possible only through divine subsistence, not as our own independent survival.
rows.anchor: eğer bunların mâverâsında bir şey ise o suretle bir bekāya nâil olacağımız ve bu bekā hakikaten bizim kendi kendimize bir bekāmız demek olmayıp ancak bekā-yı ilâhî ile mümkin olan bir bekāmız olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Our natural condition is mortality; our ultimate destiny is to endure through God in a manifestation of majesty or beauty, with eternal divine beauty as the highest aim.
rows.anchor: bizim tabîî denebilecek muktezâ-yı zâtımız fânîlik iken mukadderâtımız, nasîbimiz, bekā-billâh tarîkiyle mazhar-ı celâl veya cemâl olmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the scientific law of the persistence of cause supports this meaning: effects and partial forces vanish, while God alone, the universal cause, remains and their individual identities are preserved in divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: Fennin bekā-yı illet kānûn-ı azîminde bu mâna sâbit demektir. Maddeler, cüz’î kuvvetler hepsi ma‘luldürler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philosophers who use “spiritual subsistence” treat the human soul as though it shared divine reality and make soul survival the basis of the hereafter, thereby confusing the truth.
rows.anchor: bu vechile bekā-billâha “bekā-yı rûhânî” tâbirini kullanan feylesoflar hakīkat-i ilâhiyeyi rûh ve rûh-i beşeri hakīkat-i ilâhiyeden gibi düşündüklerinden dolayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is a mystery belonging to God’s command and its survival is possible, but making our own eternal survival the basis of the hereafter assigns us self-subsistence and forgets God as First Cause.
rows.anchor: Rûh gerçi emr-i Rab olan bir sırdır. Ve bekā-yı rûh bir emr-i münker de değildir. Fakat bizim ebediyen bekā-yı rûhumuzla bekāmıza hükmetmek bize bir bekā-yı zâtî isnad eylemektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Real is beyond spiritual and corporeal reality in a level of unity; the Lord governs the spirit that belongs to His command.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-i hak rûhâniyet ve cismâniyetin fevkinde bir mertebe-i ehadiyyettedir. Rûh emr-i Rab olmakla beraber, Rab emrine hâkimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that God prevails over His command (12:21) must not be forgotten.
rows.anchor: Rûh emr-i Rab olmakla beraber, Rab emrine hâkimdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the source and foundation of our existence and subsistence; He alone is the Living and Sustainer, and we endure through Him.
rows.anchor: bizim vücûd ve bekāmızın merci‘ü mebnâsı Allah’ın vücûd ve bekāsıdır. Biz kendi bekāmızla değil, Allah’ın bekāsıyla bâkī olabileceğiz, Hayy ü Kayyûm odur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula “We belong to God and return to Him” expresses subsistence through God.
rows.anchor: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ işte bu bekā-billâhı nâtıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is neither solely spiritual nor solely bodily survival, but the real subsistence that grounds both; the hereafter rests on it.
rows.anchor: Ve âhiret bu bekāya müsteniddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As long as God exists and endures, renewed spiritual and bodily forms remain endlessly possible.
rows.anchor: Allah mevcud ve bâkī oldukça bizim için yeniden yeniye nice nice rûhâniyetlere, cismâniyetlere mazhariyet dâima mümkin ve nâmütenâhî münkindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After death the soul may remain and be rewarded or punished in the grave and barzakh, or may itself perish later; no one can escape divine knowledge or subsistence through God, the basis of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: âlem-i kabr ve berzahta müsâb ve mu‘âteb olabilir, kalmaması ve bir müddet sonra onun da fenâya gitmesi nefsinde mümkindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hereafter is not merely survival of the soul: after barzakh there is resurrection in a distinct new creation, whose purpose is return to God in that new state.
rows.anchor: âhiret sadece bir bekā-yı rûh olmayıp hayât-ı berzahiyeden sonra başkaca bir neş’et ile ba‘s olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula asserts both a return that guarantees the hereafter and a further return in the hereafter as the highest aim and perfection.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan damân-ı âhiret olan bir rücû‘u, bir taraftan da âhirette dahi aksâ-yı emel ve gāye-i kemâl olan bir rücû‘u

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hope and fear based on subsistence through God are higher, truer, and more scientific than those based only on the theory of the soul’s survival.
rows.anchor: bekā-billâh ile ümîd ü mehâfet sadece bekā-yı rûh nazariyesine müesses ümîd ü mehâfetten çok yüksek, çok hakīkī, çok ilmîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is pure tawhid and Islam directed to God; the surah of Joseph will show that this consolation was not given to communities other than Muhammad’s.
rows.anchor: Her şâibeden müberrâ bir tevhid, bir İslâm ilallah’tır. Ve Sûre-i Yûsuf’da geleceği üzere bu tesliyet ümmet-i Muhammed’den başkasına verilmemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who rely all their hope on subsistence through God and reach the contented and approved stations deserve every glad tiding.
rows.anchor: bütün ümidini bekā-billâha istinad ettirerek râziye ve marziye makamlarına ermiş olan sâbirler her müjdeye lâyıktırlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s blessings, mercy, and guidance belong to these patient people alone.
rows.anchor: hidâyete ermiş, doğru yolu tutmuş olanlar ancak bunlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s salawat means forgiveness of all sins and bringing the patient to rewards and blessings beyond anything seen, heard, or imagined.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın Salavâtı: Bütün günahların mağfiretidir. Allah teâlâ bunların günahlarını tamamen örter ve onları rahmetiyle öyle mesûbâta, öyle nimetlere îsâl eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will be told to enter among God’s servants and enter His Garden, quoting 89:29–30.
rows.anchor: denilecektir. O sabırlar ancak îfâsı mümkin olmayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patient endurance is divine aid that covers shortcomings and sins in gratitude that cannot be fully discharged, replacing them with reward.
rows.anchor: O sabırlar ancak îfâsı mümkin olmayan şükr-i ilâhîde vâki‘olacak kusurları, günahları örtecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should seek aid through patience and prayer, attain the contented and approved stations, and face the Sacred Mosque in prayer to remember and thank God, complete promised religious and worldly blessings, and receive eternal delight in divine approval.
rows.anchor: Mü’minler bunu bilerek sabr u salât ile isti‘âne etmelidirler ve râziye vü marziye makamlarını ihraz eylemelidirler ve namazlarında Mescid-i Harâm şatrına yönelerek Allah’a zikir ve şükür eylemelidirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qibla’s sanctity also includes a communal means of remembrance, worship, and drawing near beyond prayer.
rows.anchor: Bunda namazdan başka bir tarîk-i zikr ve ibadet ve sizin için başkaca bir sûret-i ictimâ‘ve tekarrub daha vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He renders the verse: all people have one God, no other deity exists but Him, and He is the All-Merciful, the Ever-Merciful.
rows.anchor: Her hâlde hepinizin Tanrısı bir Tanrı, başka Tanrı yok ancak O. O Rahmân-ı Rahîm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All people’s true object of worship is one deity alone, unique in divinity; none other deserves worship.
rows.anchor: Ey insanlar! Hepinizin ibadet ve ubûdiyetine lâyık ve müstehak olan hakīkī mâbudunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All other objects of worship are false; no deity above, equal to, or below Him can share in divinity, which is indivisible.
rows.anchor: ulûhiyet kābil-i iştirak değildir ve bihakkın ilâh ancak o Vâhid Tanrı’dır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God has many names and attributes as the source of creation, His essence is beyond comprehension and composition.
rows.anchor: O’nun bütün mahlûkāta mebde’ olan birçok esmâsı ve sıfâtı varsa da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One’s essence cannot be described: description implies some distinction between attribute and subject, and distinction would negate absolute oneness; predication also presupposes a subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: vasıf, mevsuf ile sıfat beyninde az çok bir mugāyeret iktizâ eder. Gayriyet olunca da ferdâniyet kalmaz. Bir de ihbar bir muhberun ‘anh ile bir muhberun bih ister

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Derived names cannot reach the essence of divine oneness; at most the essence may be called “one deity” or “He,” beyond every multiplicity.
rows.anchor: esmâ-i müştakkanın hepsi hakīkat-i Hakk’ın künh-i ehadiyetine vüsûlden kāsırdır. Onun zâtına nihâyet nihâyet إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ (Hüve) denilebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine essence is not perfected by attributes; rather, the perfection of the essence entails the perfection of its attributes.
rows.anchor: Onun zâtı sıfât ile tekemmül etmiş olmayıp bilakis kemâl-i zât

rows.speaker: ehlullah
rows.claim: Among mystics immersed in tawhid, “Huwa” is highly significant and some call it the Greatest Name.
rows.anchor: Tevhid denizine dalmış olan ehlullah ‘indinde bu ismin ehemmiyeti pek büyüktür. Buna İsm-i A‘zam diyenler de vardır.

rows.speaker: İsm-i A‘zam “Allah” ism-i şerîfidir diyenler
rows.claim: More people say that the Greatest Name is the name Allah.
rows.anchor: İsm-i A‘zam “Allah” ism-i şerîfidir diyenler daha çoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Allah is more comprehensive because the name denotes the essence and all attributes together, while Huwa is greatest in the station of tawhid.
rows.anchor: “Allah” ismi, zât ve bütün sıfât mecmû‘una delâlet etmek itibariyle daha cem‘iyyetlidir. “Hüve” ise makām-ı tevhîdde a‘zamdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrases “Huwa, O Huwa, O You beyond whom none exists” are transmitted formulas of tawhid remembrance.
rows.anchor: هُو، يَا هُو، يَا مَنْ لاَ هُوَ إِلاَّ هُو tâbiri, me’sûr olan ezkâr-ı tevhîddendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one deity is the source of all multiplicity yet has no composition or multiplicity in Himself, and has no partner or equal in divinity or necessary existence.
rows.anchor: bütün kesretlerin mebde’i olmakla beraber zâtında terkib ve kesret bulunmayan, ulûhiyette, vücûb-i vücûdda hiçbir şerîk ü nazîri olmayan o İlâh vâhiddir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No creature can escape His domain, and despite His majesty He is the All-Merciful and Ever-Merciful, source of the finest compassion.
rows.anchor: dâire-i ulûhiyetinden çıkması mümkin değildir, bütün bu azamet ü kibriyâsıyla beraber O

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who associate partners with God commit shirk against the One, while those who disbelieve reject the merciful Lord and deprive themselves of eternal mercy, incurring a curse.
rows.anchor: Şirk edenler böyle bir ilâh-ı vâhide şirk etmiş, küfredenler böyle bir rahmân-ı rahîme küfretmiş oluyorlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should turn away from shirk and disbelief, believe in God and His revelations, and attain eternal mercy within tawhid.
rows.anchor: o şirk ve küfürden sarf-ı nazar etmeli de Allah’a ve Allah’ın münzelâtına iman eylemeli ve dâire-i tevhîdde bu rahmetlere ebediyyen ermelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says there were 360 idols around the Kaaba and that, on hearing the verse, the polytheists demanded a decisive proof of Muhammad’s truthfulness.
rows.anchor: üç yüz altmış tane putları vardı. Bu âyeti işittikleri zaman taaccüb ettiler

rows.speaker: Atâ
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Ata that the verse was revealed when the Prophet arrived in Medina.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr’in Atâ’dan bi’r-rivâye beyânına göre Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm Efendimiz’in Medine’ye kudûmünde

rows.speaker: Küffâr-ı Kureyş
rows.claim: The Meccan Quraysh disbelievers asked how one God could suffice for so many people; the following verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: Mekke’de küffâr-ı Kureyş “Bu kadar insanlara bir ilâh nasıl yetişir?” dediler. Bunun üzerine şu âyet nâzil oldu
